page.layout: One column of verse, set as a single poem with lines of varying length, followed by the author's name in italic capitals on a separate line at the right.

main_text.p: Quàm per vetusta seculorum scrinia Hiante oberrans lumine Minúta, magna spectet, atque casuum Notet vicissitudines. Hic prima Sanctæ jacta Gentis femina, Ritusque & actus explicat: Hic æstuosam Cæsarum impotentiam, SOLYMASQUE monstrat dirutas; Cum pingue victor hinc & hinc eques solum Sonante tundit ungula; Facesse livor. Drusius probris tuis Aut major, aut intactus est. Tibi, Serari, tabidæ Stygis Deæ Fumosa rumpant ilia. Stupes, & ora pallor ambit luteus, Mentemque percitus furis. Infane, vera quæ fit Eruditio, Quæ litterata, discito. Mirare summis Drusium parem viris, Ast æmulari desine. Haut esse vobis eruditis contigit Quotcunque rosis unguibus Barbáque sapitis. IPSA SAPIENTVM SACRA PROCVL VIDETIS INVIDI.

page.notes: No page number, running head, catchword or signature is printed. The top line is the first line of the poem, so the page is not a fragment from a prior page. Some letters are uncertain, notably the final word of line 13 ("Deæ"), which I read from a ligature. "Haut" and "Infane" are kept as printed. Spaced small capitals in "SOLYMASQUE" and "IPSA SAPIENTVM SACRA" are transcribed as capitals. Line breaks inside the verse are kept within one paragraph.
